title.en: Trump threatens to expand strikes on Iran’s civilian infrastructure next week
title.zh: 特朗普威胁下周扩大对伊朗民用基础设施的打击

summary.en: The US president has threatened to expand military strikes on Iran next week, targeting civilian infrastructure such as power plants and bridges. This threat comes amid an ongoing impasse in the Middle East crisis, with the stated aim of forcing Tehran to agree to a deal.
summary.zh: 美国总统威胁下周将扩大对伊朗的军事打击，目标包括发电厂和桥梁等民用基础设施。此举旨在迫使德黑兰在海湾地区危机僵局中达成协议。

body.en: US president says he will knock out all power plants and bridges in effort to force Tehran to agree to deal amid impasse over strait Middle East crisis – live updates Donald Trump has threatened to expand US strikes on Iran next week to target power plants and bridges if Tehran does not agree to a deal amid a continuing dispute over the strait of Hormuz. “Next week it gets really bad for them because next week comes the power plants. Next week comes the bridges,” the US president said in a Fox News interview on Tuesday. “We’re going to knock out all their power plants. We’re going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国总统表示，他将摧毁所有发电厂和桥梁，以迫使德黑兰在中东海峡危机僵局中同意达成协议——实时更新唐纳德·特朗普威胁称，如果德黑兰在霍尔木兹海峡持续争端期间不同意达成协议，美国下周将扩大对伊朗的打击，以发电厂和桥梁为目标。 “下周情况对他们来说真的很糟糕，因为下周将出现发电厂。下周将出现桥梁，”美国总统周二在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示。 “我们将摧毁他们所有的发电厂。我们将摧毁他们所有的桥梁，除非他们坐到谈判桌前进行谈判。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: In a world where leaders threaten to expand conflict and target vital infrastructure, Psalm 46:9 reminds us of Yahweh's ultimate power to make wars cease. While human intentions may lean towards destruction, we hold onto the hope that Yahweh alone can break the instruments of war and bring lasting peace.
reflection.zh: 在一个领导人威胁要扩大冲突并以重要基础设施为目标的世界上，诗篇46:9提醒我们雅伟拥有使战争止息的最终权柄。尽管人类的意图可能倾向于毁灭，我们仍持守着这样的盼望：唯有雅伟能折断争战的器械，带来持久的和平。

verse.textEn: He makes wars cease to the ends of the earth; he breaks the bow and shatters the spear.
verse.textZh: 他止息刀兵，直到地极；他折弓断枪。

title.en: Trump threatens to bomb bridges and power plants unless Iran resumes talks
title.zh: 特朗普威胁轰炸桥梁和发电厂，除非伊朗恢复谈判

summary.en: The US President has threatened to bomb Iranian infrastructure if talks do not resume, amid a four-day exchange of fire and renewed US blockades of Iranian ports.
summary.zh: 美国总统威胁称，除非伊朗恢复谈判，否则将轰炸伊朗基础设施。此前，两国已连续四天交火，美国也恢复了对伊朗港口的封锁。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump has threatened to strike Iran's bridges and power plants next week if the country does not return to talks.

The comments, made in a Fox News interview, aired as the two countries exchanged fire for the fourth day in a row.

Trump earlier reversed a threat of a 20% fee on all Strait of Hormuz cargo shipping but resumed blockading Iranian ports.

"Next week it gets really bad for them," Trump said. "We're going to knock out all their power plants. We're going to knock out all their bridges unless they get to the table and negotiate."

Back in April, Trump threatened to bomb civilian infrastructure in Iran, including bridges and power plants.

UN human rights chief Volker Türk responded at the time by saying: "Under international law, deliberately attacking civilians and civilian infrastructure is a war crime."

The 1949 Geneva Conventions on humanitarian conduct in war prohibit attacks on sites considered essential for civilians.

"I'll save the energy targets for last, but ultimately we'll hit energy targets," Trump said in an interview on Special Report with Bret Baier that aired on Tuesday night.

He said US negotiators had conveyed to their Iranian counterparts on Tuesday evening that they "'better make a deal, or you're not going to have anything left'".

The escalation in rhetoric comes after Trump said a 20% toll he had threatened to impose in the Strait of Hormuz would be replaced by "massive" trade and investment deals with Gulf states.

The announcement came hours before the US military carried out a seven-hour wave of strikes on Iran and resumed a blockade of its ports.

US Central Command (Centcom) said "dozens" of Iranian military targets near the Strait of Hormuz, with the aim to "further degrade Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping and civilian crews".

Meanwhile, Tehran fired missiles and drones on US targets in Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain, Iranian state-run television IRIB reported.

In the early hours of Wednesday, Kuwait's military said it was intercepting Iranian attack drones, while Bahrain activated air raid sirens.

"Kuwaiti air defences are currently engaging hostile drone attacks following the nefarious Iranian aggression," the Kuwaiti army said. Bahrain's interior ministry urged citizens and residents to remain calm and head to the nearest safe place.

The US also said Iran had "intentionally targeted civilians" in the region by attacking seven commercial ships, which had resulted in "nearly a dozen civilian crew members killed, missing, or injured", the commander of Centcom said in a statement late on Tuesday.

body.zh: 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普威胁称，如果伊朗不重返谈判，下周将袭击伊朗的桥梁和发电厂。 这一评论是在福克斯新闻采访中发表的，当时两国已连续第四天交火。 特朗普早些时候推翻了对霍尔木兹海峡所有货物运输征收 20% 费用的威胁，但恢复封锁伊朗港口。 特朗普说：“下周对他们来说情况会变得非常糟糕。” “我们将摧毁他们所有的发电厂。我们将摧毁他们所有的桥梁，除非他们坐到谈判桌前进行谈判。” 早在四月份，特朗普就威胁要轰炸伊朗的民用基础设施，包括桥梁和发电厂。 联合国人权事务高级专员沃尔克·蒂尔克当时回应说：“根据国际法，故意攻击平民和民用基础设施是战争罪。” 1949 年关于战争中人道主义行为的日内瓦公约禁止袭击被认为对平民至关重要的场所。 “我会把能源目标留到最后，但最终我们会实现能源目标，”特朗普在周二晚间播出的布雷特·拜尔特别报道采访中表示。 他说，美国谈判代表周二晚间已向伊朗谈判代表表示，他们“最好达成协议，否则你将一无所有”。 在特朗普表示他威胁要在霍尔木兹海峡征收20%的通行费将被与海湾国家的“大规模”贸易和投资协议所取代之后，言论升级。 这一消息是在美国军方对伊朗进行长达七小时的打击并恢复对其港口的封锁之前几个小时宣布的。 美国中央司令部（Centcom）表示，霍尔木兹海峡附近有“数十个”伊朗军事目标，目的是“进一步削弱伊朗威胁商业航运和民用船员的能力”。 与此同时，据伊朗国营电视台 IRIB 报道，德黑兰向约旦、科威特和巴林的美国目标发射了导弹和无人机。 周三凌晨，科威特军方表示正在拦截伊朗的攻击无人机，而巴林则拉响了空袭警报。 科威特军方表示：“在伊朗的邪恶侵略之后，科威特防空系统目前正在对敌方无人机发起攻击。”巴林内政部敦促公民和居民保持冷静，前往最近的安全地点。 美国还表示，伊朗袭击了七艘商船，“故意针对该地区的平民”，导致“近十几名平民船员死亡、失踪或受伤”，中央司令部司令在周二晚间的一份声明中表示。 阿拉伯联合酋长国（阿联酋）周一晚间表示，伊朗巡航导弹瞄准了两艘国家油轮，造成一名印度船员死亡，另有八人受伤，其中四人……

reflection.en: In times of escalating tension and threats of violence, the call to pursue peace can feel distant. Yet, Yahweh's word reminds us of our responsibility to seek peaceful coexistence whenever possible. This story highlights the profound challenge of maintaining peace when diplomatic efforts falter and threats loom.
reflection.zh: 在紧张局势升级和暴力威胁加剧的时刻，追求和平的呼召可能显得遥远。然而，雅伟的话语提醒我们，只要可能，就有责任寻求和平共处。这个故事凸显了当外交努力受挫、威胁逼近时，维持和平所面临的严峻挑战。

verse.textEn: If it is possible, as far as it depends on you, live at peace with everyone.
verse.textZh: 若是能行，总要尽力与众人和睦。

title.en: Volodymyr Zelenskyy pushes for new government in Ukraine
title.zh: 弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基推动乌克兰组建新政府

summary.en: Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko has resigned after serving for just over a year. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is now engaging in discussions to identify and appoint her potential successors, prompting questions about the future direction of the Cabinet.
summary.zh: 乌克兰总理尤利娅·斯维里登科在任职一年多后辞职。总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基正在与潜在继任者进行谈判，这引发了人们对内阁未来走向的疑问。

body.en:
Ukrainian Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko stepped down after barely a year in office. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is already in talks with potential successors. What can Ukraine expect from the Cabinet reshuffle?

On Tuesday, Ukraine's parliament approved Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko's   resignation  with a clear majority, dismissing the country's entire government.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy  had announced on social media on Sunday that he had offered Svyrydenko a new position. Media report that she could become Ukraine's next ambassador to the United States.

"I am grateful to Yulia for her clear, steady and effective work as prime minister, and for all her years of successful work as part of Team Ukraine ," Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram. "I have offered her the opportunity to take on a new significant role in relations with an important partner. I expect that, together with members of parliament, we will make the necessary changes to the Ukrainian government."

Zelenskyy posted photos of meetings with Sergii Koretskyi, head of the state-owned energy company Naftogaz, first Deputy Prime Minister and Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal , Interior Minister Ihor Klymenko, Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov and Kharkiv Mayor Ihor Terekhov.

There has been much speculation and debate about why Zelenskyy might be reshuffling the government, which has been in office for less than a year . Ihor Reiterovych, a political scientist with the Taras Shevchenko National University in Kyiv, told DW that a reshuffle had originally been planned for the coming fall or spring. However, Reiterovych said, several recent incidents had prompted a more immediate intervention.

Mainly, there is the issue of Ukraine's current ambassador to the United States : Olga Stefanishyna. She is  being investigated  by Ukraine's anti-corruption authorities regarding activities prior to her appointment to work in Washington, DC. There are rumors that she is considering resigning. "It is possible that the Americans signaled that a scandal involving the ambassador would be too much for them and that something needed to be done," Reiterovych said. "That's why Zelenskyy had to react. Svyrydenko is a good candidate; she cooperated well on the raw materials agreement with the Americans and established contacts there. The Americans are willing to work with people with whom they've already worked together."

Reiterovych said recent scandals involving the armed forces could damage Zelenskyy's  reputation as Ukraine's commander-in-chief. Investigative reporting has uncovered instances of torture, the cruel treatment of recruits and the cover-up of deaths occurring outside of combat operations. At the same time, inspections are underway...
body.zh: 乌克兰总理尤利娅·斯维里登科上任不到一年就辞职了。总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基已经在与潜在的继任者进行谈判。乌克兰对内阁改组有何期待？ 周二，乌克兰议会以绝对多数票批准了总理尤利娅·斯维里登科的辞职，解散了该国整个政府。 乌克兰总统泽连斯基周日在社交媒体上宣布，他为斯维里登科提供了一个新职位。媒体报道称她可能成为乌克兰下一任驻美国大使。 泽连斯基在 Telegram 上写道：“我感谢尤利娅作为总理所做的清晰、稳定和有效的工作，以及她多年来作为乌克兰队一员所做的成功工作。” “我为她提供了在与重要合作伙伴的关系中发挥新的重要作用的机会。我希望与议会成员一起，我们将对乌克兰政府做出必要的改变。” 泽连斯基发布了与国有能源公司 Naftogaz 总裁谢尔盖·科列茨基 (Sergii Koretskyi)、第一副总理兼能源部长丹尼斯·什米哈尔 (Denys Shmyhal)、内政部长伊霍尔·克利门科 (Ihor Klymenko)、国防部长米哈伊洛·费多罗夫 (Mykhailo Fedorov) 和哈尔科夫市市长伊霍尔·捷列霍夫 (Ihor Terekhov) 会面的照片。 关于泽连斯基为何要对上任不到一年的政府进行改组，存在很多猜测和争论。基辅塔拉斯·舍甫琴科国立大学政治学家伊霍尔·雷特罗维奇 (Ihor Reiterovych) 告诉德国之声，改组最初计划于明年秋季或春季进行。然而，雷特罗维奇表示，最近发生的几起事件促使我们立即采取干预措施。 主要是乌克兰现任驻美国大使奥尔加·斯特凡尼西娜（Olga Stefanishyna）的问题。乌克兰反腐败机构正在对她在被任命到华盛顿特区工作之前的活动进行调查。有传言称她正在考虑辞职。 “美国人可能表示，涉及大使的丑闻对他们来说太过分了，需要采取一些措施，”雷特罗维奇说。 “这就是泽伦斯基必须做出反应的原因。斯维里登科是一个很好的候选人；她在原材料协议上与美国人合作良好，并在那里建立了联系。美国人愿意与他们已经合作过的人合作。” 雷特罗维奇表示，最近涉及武装部队的丑闻可能会损害泽伦斯基作为乌克兰总司令的声誉。调查报告揭露了酷刑、残酷对待新兵以及掩盖战斗行动之外发生的死亡事件。与此同时，检查工作正在进行中……

reflection.en: As Ukraine faces a government reshuffle, the character of its leaders becomes paramount for the nation's future. Proverbs 29:2 reminds us that when righteous leaders thrive, the people rejoice, but when the wicked rule, the people groan. This moment calls for discernment in choosing those who will serve with integrity and wisdom for the good of all.
reflection.zh: 随着乌克兰面临政府改组，其领导人的品格对国家未来至关重要。箴言29:2提醒我们，义人掌权，百姓就欢喜；恶人掌权，百姓就叹息。此刻，需要明辨地选择那些将以正直和智慧为全民福祉服务的人。

verse.textEn: When the righteous thrive, the people rejoice; when the wicked rule, the people groan.
verse.textZh: 义人增多，民就喜乐；恶人掌权，民就叹息。

title.en: England risks building new ‘death traps’ as experts warn of overheating crisis
title.zh: 英格兰面临建造新‘死亡陷阱’的风险，专家警告过热危机

summary.en: Research indicates that only half of local authority plans in England include cooling strategies, leading experts to warn that new buildings risk becoming "death traps" due to overheating. This oversight puts vulnerable people at increased risk unless the government strengthens building standards and prioritizes...
summary.zh: 研究显示，英格兰只有一半的地方政府规划要求采取降温策略，专家警告称，新建筑可能因过热而成为“死亡陷阱”。除非政府收紧标准并优先考虑气候因素，否则这一疏忽将使弱势群体面临更大的风险。

body.en: Vulnerable people more at risk as research finds only half of local authority plans require cooling strategies England risks constructing a new generation of “death trap” buildings that can fatally overheat unless the government tightens standards and prioritises climate safeguards, planning experts have said. Fears are growing about the plight of vulnerable people in heatwaves, with research this week suggesting that 2,700 people had died in the May and June heatwaves in England and Wales. Yet only about half of local plans being drawn up by councils and local authorities require new buildings to have a cooling or ventilation strategy to prevent overheating, according to findings from the Royal Town Planning Institute (RTPI) and the Town and Country Planning Association (TCPA). Continue reading...
body.zh: 研究发现，只有一半的地方当局计划需要降温策略，弱势群体面临的风险更大。规划专家表示，英国面临着建造新一代“死亡陷阱”建筑的风险，这些建筑可能会因过热而致命，除非政府收紧标准并优先考虑气候保障措施。人们越来越担心热浪中弱势群体的困境，本周的研究表明英格兰和威尔士有 2,700 人在 5 月和 6 月的热浪中死亡。然而，根据皇家城市规划研究所 (RTPI) 和城乡规划协会 (TCPA) 的调查结果，只有大约一半的地方议会和地方当局制定的地方规划要求新建筑采取冷却或通风策略，以防止过热。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report highlights a critical need for foresight and responsible planning to protect the vulnerable from foreseeable dangers. Yahweh's wisdom reminds us that prudence involves seeing danger and taking action, lest negligence leads to suffering. It calls those in authority to heed warnings and build with care for all, especially the most susceptible.
reflection.zh: 这份报告强调了预见性和负责任的规划对于保护弱势群体免受可预见危险的关键需求。雅伟的智慧提醒我们，审慎在于预见危险并采取行动，以免疏忽导致苦难。它呼吁当权者听取警告，并为所有人，特别是最易受影响的人，谨慎建造。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Wednesday briefing: ​Do MPs have the will to stop mega-donors interfering in UK politics?
title.zh: 周三简报：议员们是否有意愿阻止巨额捐款干预英国政治？

summary.en: A UK parliamentary bill aimed at curbing the influence of large political donations has become a key test of the nation's ability to limit interference from wealthy individuals in its political system. The legislation seeks to address the growing concern over billionaire-backed contributions influencing national...
summary.zh: 一项旨在遏制大额政治捐款影响的英国议会法案，已成为检验该国能否限制富豪干预政治制度的关键考验。该立法旨在解决人们日益担忧的亿万富翁资助的捐款对国家治理产生影响的问题。

reflection.zh: 巨额捐款影响政治的挑战，凸显了财富与公共服务之间持久的张力。雅伟的话语提醒我们，贪财是万恶之根，可能使领袖偏离服务所有公民的职责。维护治理的廉洁需要警惕此类诱惑。

title.en: China economic growth falls sharply, missing target
title.zh: 中国经济增长大幅放缓，未能达到目标

summary.en: China's economic growth has significantly slowed, failing to meet its targets. This downturn is attributed to weak domestic demand and the impact of the Iran war on global oil prices, despite strong export performance.
summary.zh: 中国经济增长大幅放缓，未能达到预期目标。尽管出口表现强劲，但国内需求疲软以及伊朗战争对油价的影响，共同导致了此次经济下滑。

body.en:
China's economic growth slowed sharply between the start of April and end of June as weak domestic demand and the Iran war's impact on oil prices overshadowed the country's strong exports.

Official gross domestic product (GDP) figures showed the world's second largest economy grew in the second quarter by 4.3%, below Beijing's annual target, and after a 5% rise in the first quarter.

It comes a day after government data showed that China's exports jumped by 27% in June compared to a year earlier.

In March, China cut the growth target to a range of 4.5%-5% , its lowest economic expansion goal since 1991, a move some analysts say gives officials more flexibility in managing the economy.

The announcement represents the first full quarter of GDP data since the start of the Iran war on 28 February and marks the lowest quarterly expansion since the end of 2022, as China was emerging from its strict Covid-19 restrictions.

"The are more external instability and uncertainty factors," China's National Bureau of Statistics said in a release accompanying the figures.

It also noted an imbalance between strong supply and weak demand in the domestic economy.

Separate data released on Wednesday highlighted the economic challenges Beijing is facing at home - including a long-running property market slump and weak consumer spending.

New home prices contracted again, although the 0.1% fall in June was at a slightly slower pace than the previous month.

Fabien Yip, a market analyst at investment platform IG told the BBC that China's businesses are absorbing higher energy and raw materials costs "because demand at the till is too weak to bear it".

The situation will become more difficult to manage the longer the Iran war goes on, she added.

Customs data for June, which was released on Tuesday, showed that China's tech exports were boosted by soaring global demand for semiconductors to power artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

Surging demand for Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) also gave a major boost to China's exports - with monthly car exports topping one million for the first time.
body.zh: 由于国内需求疲软和伊朗战争对油价的影响掩盖了中国强劲的出口，中国的经济增长在四月初至六月底大幅放缓。 官方国内生产总值(GDP)数据显示，继第一季度增长5%之后，世界第二大经济体第二季度增长4.3%，低于北京的年度目标。 一天前，政府数据显示，中国 6 月份出口同比增长 27%。 3月份，中国将增长目标下调至4.5%-5%，这是自1991年以来的最低经济扩张目标，一些分析师表示，此举让官员在管理经济方面拥有更大的灵活性。 该公告代表了自 2 月 28 日伊朗战争爆发以来第一个完整季度的 GDP 数据，也标志着中国正在摆脱严格的 Covid-19 限制之际，自 2022 年底以来的最低季度扩张。 “外部不稳定和不确定因素较多，”中国国家统计局在发布的数据中表示。 报告还指出，国内经济供给旺盛与需求疲软之间存在不平衡。 周三公布的另一份数据突显了北京在国内面临的经济挑战，包括房地产市场长期低迷和消费者支出疲软。 新房价格再次收缩，但 6 月份降幅为 0.1%，降幅较上月略有放缓。 投资平台IG的市场分析师Fabien Yip告诉BBC，中国企业正在吸收更高的能源和原材料成本，“因为收银台的需求太弱而无法承受”。 她补充说，伊朗战争持续的时间越长，局势就越难以控制。 周二公布的 6 月份海关数据显示，全球对为人工智能 (AI) 数据中心提供动力的半导体需求飙升，推动了中国的科技出口。 中国电动汽车（EV）需求的激增也极大地推动了中国的出口——每月汽车出口量首次突破100万辆。

reflection.en: Economic reports often highlight human efforts and global factors in prosperity, yet this news reminds us that even the most robust plans can be affected by unforeseen circumstances. It prompts reflection on the ultimate source of our ability to create wealth and sustain well-being, which Yahweh provides.
reflection.zh: 经济报告常强调人类努力和全球因素对繁荣的影响，但这则新闻提醒我们，即使是最周密的计划也可能受不可预见的情况影响。它促使我们反思创造财富和维持福祉能力的最终来源，这能力由雅伟赐予。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: 'Completely disfigured': Wife recalls experience as husband sucked out of Ryanair plane
title.zh: “完全毁容”：妻子回忆丈夫被瑞安航空飞机吸出机舱的经历

summary.en: Both Greek prosecutors and air accident investigators have launched investigations into how a window became dislodged on a Ryanair plane, an incident during which a husband was reportedly sucked out and left "completely disfigured."
summary.zh: 希腊检察官和航空事故调查人员已对瑞安航空一架飞机窗户脱落的事件展开调查，据报道，在此事件中，一名丈夫被吸出机舱，导致“完全毁容”。

body.en:
Svetlana Maksimovic and her husband Ljubisa Karovic had ‌just settled into a Ryanair flight when a loud bang pierced the hum of engines.

Within seconds, she saw her 61-year-old husband being ‌sucked out of the plane through a dislodged cabin window.

In what Greek officials have described as a rare incident, Karovic, sitting in a window seat, was pulled through the window as his wife and others held on to him on the flight between the Greek city of Thessaloniki and Germany on 10 July.

"I've never heard anything louder in my life before. I just turned around and saw ‌that part of ‌his body had ⁠already gone out the window," Maksimovic told Reuters.

Karovic is now being treated in hospital in Thessaloniki with severe neck and arm injuries.

Greek media and airport sources said that a piece of engine likely broke off and smashed a window early in the flight, causing the cabin to decompress.

Boeing says it's assisting the investigation, being led by North Macedonia, over which the incident occurred.

The US National Transportation Safety Board and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency are involved in the investigation.

A Greek prosecutor has also launched a probe into the ⁠case, while Greek air accident investigators are also looking into it. The aircraft is still ‌in Greece.

"What happened was extremely serious," ‌the couple's legal adviser, Vassilis Tsiaras, said, adding that the pending results of the probe were pivotal.

Ryanair, which has confirmed that a window dislodged during the flight, said it would not comment further while the incident is under formal investigation.

After takeoff, Karovic was relaxed and had probably fallen asleep, Maksimovic said.

She said that after the loud bang occurred, a woman sitting next to her husband kept pulling his left arm but it was only after another passenger came to help that ‌they succeeded in getting him back inside the plane, which had by then started to descend.

Maksimovic, who had left her seat to help her husband, put an oxygen mask on him while another passenger gave her one for her own use.

"His face was completely disfigured, there was blood everywhere and his ears, eyes, nose were completely deformed," she said, adding that her husband was still struggling to recover.

"How we're going to heal and how long that treatment will last and in what way, we'll see."

body.zh: 斯维特兰娜·马克西莫维奇 (Svetlana Maksimovic) 和她的丈夫柳比萨·卡罗维奇 (Ljubisa Karovic) 刚刚搭乘瑞安航空 (Ryanair) 的航班，突然一声巨响刺穿了发动机的嗡嗡声。 几秒钟之内，她看到 61 岁的丈夫被从脱落的机舱窗户中吸出飞机。 希腊官员称这是一起罕见的事件，7月10日，在希腊城市塞萨洛尼基和德国之间的航班上，坐在靠窗座位上的卡罗维奇被他的妻子和其他人拉着从窗户拉了出去。 “我以前从未听到过比这更响亮的声音。我转过身，发现他身体的一部分已经消失在窗外，”马克西莫维奇告诉路透社。 您值得信赖的来源，让您了解周围世界的最新动态。直接将免费的每日新闻更新和分析发送到您的收件箱。 卡罗维奇因颈部和手臂严重受伤，目前正在塞萨洛尼基的医院接受治疗。 希腊媒体和机场消息人士称，航班起飞初期，一个发动机的一块可能断裂并砸碎了窗户，导致机舱减压。 波音公司表示，正在协助此次事件发生的北马其顿领导的调查。 美国国家运输安全委员会和欧盟航空安全局参与调查。 希腊检察官也已对此案展开调查，希腊空难调查人员也在调查此事。这架飞机仍在希腊。 “发生的事情非常严重，”这对夫妇的法律顾问瓦西利斯·齐亚拉斯（Vassilis Tsiaras）说，并补充说，悬而未决的调查结果至关重要。 瑞安航空已证实飞行过程中有一扇窗户脱落，并表示在事件正在接受正式调查期间不会进一步发表评论。 马克西莫维奇说，起飞后，卡罗维奇很放松，可能已经睡着了。 她说，巨响发生后，坐在她丈夫旁边的一名女子不断拉扯他的左臂，但直到另一名乘客过来帮忙后，他们才成功将他带回飞机内，当时飞机已经开始下降。 马克西莫维奇离开座位去帮助丈夫，给他戴上氧气面罩，另一名乘客则给了她一个供她自己使用。 “他的脸完全毁容，到处都是血，他的耳朵、眼睛、鼻子完全变形了，”她说，并补充说她的丈夫仍在努力康复。 “我们将如何治愈、治疗将持续多长时间以及以何种方式进行，我们拭目以待。” 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: The terrifying experience of being sucked from a plane, leaving one "completely disfigured," speaks to moments in life when we face pressures far beyond our human ability to endure. In such overwhelming circumstances, even the strongest among us can despair of life itself. Yet, even in the deepest anguish, we are reminded that Yahweh understands our limits...
reflection.zh: 被吸出飞机并“完全毁容”的恐怖经历，揭示了生命中我们面临远超人类承受能力的巨大压力。在这样压倒性的境况中，即使是最坚强的人也可能对生命感到绝望。然而，即使在最深的痛苦中，我们也当记得雅伟理解我们的极限，并与我们一同承受苦难。

verse.textEn: We were under great pressure, far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired of life itself.
verse.textZh: 我们被压太重，力不能胜，甚至连活命的指望都绝了。

title.en: China detains US scientist who studied North Korea nuclear tests
title.zh: 中国拘留研究朝鲜核试验的美国科学家

summary.en: A US scientist, Chen Youlin, has been detained in China for nearly two years on spying charges, according to his family, who claim his detention is wrongful.
summary.zh: 据陈友林家人称，这位美国科学家在中国被拘留近两年，面临间谍指控，家人表示他被错误拘留。

body.en:
China has detained a US seismologist who tracks nuclear tests for nearly two years on espionage charges, his family says.

Chen Youlin, 54, was arrested in November 2024 during a trip to Beijing to visit family, according to hostage advocacy group Global Reach. The family decided to speak out after they saw no sign of Beijing freeing Chen.

His wife Rong Yufang, also a seismologist, said Chen worked closely with Chinese colleagues, and the allegations are "both wrong and inconsistent with the public and collaborative nature of the work that he has done".

His published work centres on North Korea, a close friend of China and long sanctioned for its nuclear weapons programme and underground tests.

It is unclear if and how Chen's work touched on Beijing's nuclear programme. US intelligence suggests that China is developing a new arsenal and has conducted secret tests, which Beijing denies.

When asked about the case at a daily press briefing on Tuesday, China's foreign ministry said its "judicial authorities handle cases in accordance with the law".

"There is no such thing as so-called wrongful detention," the ministry's spokesman Lin Jian said. In China, espionage convictions can lead to life imprisonment or death.

"I have not been able to speak with my husband for over 600 days and am concerned for his health and well-being," Rong said in a statement through Global Reach.

In an interview with Reuters, she said Chinese authorities interrogated her husband more than 100 times on his work and that he wasn't allowed to see a lawyer for the first 13 months of his detention.

Born in China, Chen became a US citizens in 2011. He lives in Boston, Massachusetts.

He specialised in using seismological data to identify nuclear tests, and undertook several projects funded by the US government. Rong said he his work with colleagues in China was always done "transparently".

"He is doing precisely the kind of people-to-people engagement that the Chinese government says it wants," she added.

Chen's work included a study in December 2020 that looked at seismic data recorded across Asia, including China, to improve methods for nuclear-test monitoring and yield estimation.

According to Global Reach, there are "suspicions within the US government that Chen's arrest was spurred by China's conduct of nuclear tests in violation of the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty".

The group said Chen's expertise would give China "an opportunity to learn as much as possible about US seismic detection methodologies so they can establish countermeasures that allow them to circumvent the treaty".

title.en: Seven Britons among those killed in Spain wildfires
title.zh: 七名英国公民在西班牙森林大火中丧生

summary.en: Spanish authorities reported that seven Britons were among the thirteen victims killed in recent wildfires, with twelve of the deceased identified as foreign nationals.
summary.zh: 西班牙当局周二表示，在近期森林大火中遇难的13人中，有7名英国公民，共有12名遇难者是外国公民。

body.en:
Seven Britons were among those killed in the deadly wildfires in southern Spain, authorities have confirmed.

Twelve of the 13 victims were foreign nationals, Spanish authorities said on Tuesday after completing post-mortem examinations, according to local media and Agence France Presse (AFP).

The wildfires, which tore through Spain's Almería province on Thursday, have become one of the country's deadliest.

A spokesperson for the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office previously said it was "supporting British nationals affected and their families and remain in close contact with the Spanish authorities".

In a statement, officials said seven of the victims were from the United Kingdom, three from Belgium, one from France and another from the United States, as cited by AFP and local media.

"The 13 people who died are eight women and five men, all adults," the public body responsible for identifying the victims added.

Among the British nationals who died were couple Pete and Fran Gillam, who lived in Bédar, the village that bore the brunt of the wildfires. Their deaths were confirmed by their family.

Posting on Facebook, their daughter Danielle Gillam-Kirton, from Sheffield, said the family were "heartbroken to share that we have received confirmation from the police that Mum and Dad did not survive the fire".

Nearly 1,500 people were evacuated from Almería province as firefighters battled the flames.

British man Malcolm Timbrell, 70, who lives in the village of Bédar and survived the fires, spoke to the BBC outside his destroyed home high on the hillside.

His wife and friends are believed to be among those killed during the wildfires.

Timbrell described the moment he was separated from the group, and attempted to take refuge in some abandoned cars: "Of the six cars, four of them instantly combusted and as each one started to go, I moved back one car.

"For some reason of fate, the last two cars, although very, very badly singed and paint bubbled and burnt, survived.

Spain has suffered frequent and severe heatwaves in recent years, with temperatures often exceeding 40C.

The fire, which has now been contained, burned through about 7,000 hectares (17,300 acres) of land, authorities said.
body.zh: 当局证实，西班牙南部致命山火中有七名英国人丧生。 据当地媒体和法新社报道，西班牙当局在完成尸检后于周二表示，13 名遇难者中有 12 人是外国人。 周四席卷西班牙阿尔梅里亚省的野火已成为该国最致命的火灾之一。 英国外交、联邦与发展办公室发言人此前表示，“正在支持受影响的英国国民及其家人，并与西班牙当局保持密切联系”。 据法新社和当地媒体援引，官员们在一份声明中表示，其中七名受害者来自英国，三名来自比利时，一名来自法国，另一名来自美国。 负责确认遇难者身份的公共机构补充道：“13 名死者中有 8 名女性和 5 名男性，均为成年人。” 遇难的英国公民包括皮特·吉拉姆 (Pete Gillam) 和弗兰·吉拉姆 (Fran Gillam) 夫妇，他们住在贝达尔 (Bédar) 村，该村在野火中首当其冲。他们的死亡得到了家人的证实。 来自谢菲尔德的女儿丹妮尔·吉拉姆-科顿在脸书上发帖称，全家人“心碎地告诉大家，我们已收到警方的确认，妈妈和爸爸在火灾中不幸身亡”。 消防队员与大火搏斗时，阿尔梅里亚省近 1,500 人被疏散。 70 岁的英国男子马尔科姆·廷布雷尔 (Malcolm Timbrell) 住在贝达尔 (Bédar) 村，在大火中幸存下来，他在山坡上被毁的房屋外接受了 BBC 采访。 据信他的妻子和朋友也在野火中丧生。 蒂姆布雷尔描述了他与人群分开的那一刻，并试图躲进一些废弃的汽车中：“六辆车中，其中四辆立即燃烧，当每辆汽车开始离开时，我向后移了一辆车。 “由于某种命运的原因，最后两辆车虽然被烧得非常非常严重，油漆起泡并被烧毁，但还是幸存了下来。 西班牙近年来遭遇频繁且严重的热浪天气，气温经常超过40℃。 当局表示，火势现已得到控制，烧毁了约 7,000 公顷（17,300 英亩）的土地。

title.en: US reimpose Strait of Hormuz blockade as strikes stall peace talks
title.zh: 美国重新实施霍尔木兹海峡封锁，罢工使和平谈判陷入僵局

summary.en: The United States has reimposed a blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, marking the second time this year, as ongoing strikes have caused peace talks to stall.

body.en:
United States forces carried out strikes against Iran for a fourth day in a row on Wednesday and reimposed a naval blockade to prevent ships from sailing to or from the country's ports.

The military action came after US President Donald Trump backed down on his threat to heavily tax ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz , saying Gulf countries had agreed to make major investments in the US.

US Central Command (CENTCOM) said the latest strikes were aimed at "degrading Iranian capabilities used to attack commercial shipping" in the strait, the key shipping channel for Gulf oil and gas where Iran has repeatedly carried out attacks on civilian vessels.

Iranian state media reported explosions near the port city of Bandar Abbas, on the Gulf island of Qeshm near the Strait of Hormuz, and other locations.

The renewed naval blockade came into force at 6am AEST on Wednesday — an hour after the US strikes began — with a senior Iranian official saying the move effectively wrecked a deal struck to pause the conflict to allow peace talks to take place.

"There are currently more than 20 US Navy warships and hundreds of military aircraft operating across the Middle East," CENTCOM said in a post announcing the resumption of the blockade, adding: "American forces remain vigilant, lethal, and ready."

On Tuesday, Iran said a previous round of US strikes targeted Qeshm, while local authorities also said US forces struck "four points" in Bushehr — which hosts Iran's only civilian nuclear power plant — as well as an Iranian border area near Iraq and Kuwait.

Iran, in turn, hit two ships in the Strait of Hormuz, killing two crew members, according to the International Maritime Organisation.

A Norwegian tanker was also hit by an explosion caused by an unidentified device off the Omani coast on Tuesday, the crisis response company MTI Network said.

Kuwait said one of its naval vessels was struck during an Iranian missile and drone barrage, wounding four crew members.

Trump, meanwhile, said he was scrapping a planned levy on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz that he announced on Tuesday, replacing the fee with trade deals with Gulf allies.

"I have decided to replace the 20 per cent United States Reimbursement Fee with Trade and Investment Deals that the various Gulf States will be making into the United States," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.

Since last week, renewed US attacks have killed at least 28 people in Iran, according to an AFP tally based on Iranian media and official announcements.

title.en: Trump retreat over Hormuz tolls suggests he is struggling to end Iran war
title.zh: 特朗普在霍尔木兹海峡问题上的退让，表明他正努力结束与伊朗的战争

summary.en: The US president's sudden policy reversal marked the latest development in a conflict that has persisted for over four months.
summary.zh: 美国总统突然改变政策，是这场已持续四个多月的冲突中的最新转折。

body.en:
Donald Trump's latest Iran War demand lasted all of 24 hours and suggests a president searching for unorthodox ways out of a difficult position.

On Monday morning, in a social media post announcing the resumption of an American naval blockade on Iranian shipping, he said that all vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz - including those of US allies - must pay a 20% fee to reimburse the US "for any and all costs necessary to do the job of providing safety and security to this very volatile section of the world".

The following day, he abandoned that proposal completely , external , offering instead that he would strike "trade and investment deals" with America's Gulf allies, implying the US would offer them safe passage through the Strait in return.

The abrupt about-face was the latest twist in a conflict that has now lasted more than four months and, despite a month old "memorandum of understanding" that secured a temporary ceasefire and set up a framework for negotiations, shows no sign of ending.

Trump may be reluctant to escalate the war given its continued unpopularity, the likelihood of rising energy prices and the risks associated with America forces and allies once again coming under Iranian attack. He might find the prospect of ending the conflict without reaching an agreement he can claim is better than the one Barack Obama's administration negotiated in 2015 also distasteful, however.

"I think the most likely ending is a non-ending," Rosemary Kelanic, Director of the Middle East program at Defense Priorities, said. "This has turned into a war of attrition, and wars of attrition tend to go on for a long, long period of time."

The US-Iran memorandum of understanding (MOU) - and the hopes that came with it for an end to the war - died at 10:16 ET (16:16 BST) on Tuesday on Truth Social, when Trump announced a resumption of the US blockade of Iranian shipping, amidst a flurry of new US military strikes on targets across Iran.

The Iranians countered by stepping up attacks on US allies and commercial shipping in the region, grinding traffic through the Strait of Hormuz to a near standstill once more.

After nearly a month of on-again, off-again negotiations between the two nations, punctuated by occasional hostilities that tested the definition of a "ceasefire", Trump and the Americans appear to be facing the same challenges that had been present through much of the Iran War.

While militarily, the Americans were achieving their objectives, as measured in Iranian ships, planes and targets destroyed and defence capabilities degraded, politically the conflict was far from resolved.

title.zh: 2016年政变企图如何永久改变了土耳其

summary.en: Ten years ago, a faction within the Turkish military attempted to overthrow President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's government. The failed coup's repercussions have profoundly and permanently altered Turkey's political landscape.
summary.zh: 十年前，土耳其军方部分人员试图推翻总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安的政府。这场未遂政变的后果至今仍在深刻地、永久地塑造着土耳其的政治格局。

body.en:
Ten years ago, parts of the Turkish military attempted to overthrow the government of President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The consequences of the failed coup continue to shape Turkey to this day. DW looks back.

It was the evening of July 15, 2016. A warm summer day was coming to an end. Many people were spending their Friday evening with friends or family, looking forward to the weekend. There was nothing to suggest that  Turkey  was about to be fundamentally transformed.

Then, just a few hours later, tanks were rolling through the streets. Fighter jets flying over Ankara and Istanbul. Soldiers blocking the Bosphorus Bridge, the link between Europe and Asia. The parliament in Ankara came under fire. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called on the public via a video call broadcast to take to the streets and stop the coup.

The coup attempt failed that very night, but its political consequences continue to influence the country to this day .

The Turkish government blamed the Gulen movement for the coup attempt. Its founder, the Muslim cleric Fethullah Gulen , was once considered a close ally of Erdogan. Together, they played a key role in curbing the political influence of the Turkish military and expanding Erdogan's power. Later, the alliance fell apart .

By 2016, Gulen had been living in exile in the United States for years. The government accused Gulen of having infiltrated the judiciary, police, military, and other state institutions with followers over decades in an effort to undermine the state. Gulen and his followers denied any involvement in the coup. Many high-ranking military officials with alleged ties to Gulen were arrested. Gulen died  aged 83 in the US in 2024.

In Turkey, July 15 is now a national holiday. The former Bosphorus Bridge was renamed the "Bridge of the Martyrs of July 15." It commemorates the people who lost their lives that night. According to official figures, 253 people died, most of them civilians. Many streets, squares and schools also bear the name "July 15".

However, the anniversary is not just about commemorating the victims. It also marks a profound political turning point. The Gulen movement was designated a terrorist organization, and its alleged supporters were largely extracted from the state apparatus.

Six days after the coup, parliament approved a state of emergency. It was initially limited to three months but was extended seven times and did not end until July 19, 2018. During those two years, the president governed largely by emergency decrees, issuing 32 decrees in total.

The consequences of these political purges have been enormous. More than 125,000 members of the civil service and the armed forces were dismissed . According to official figures, approximately...
body.zh: 十年前，土耳其军队的部分人员试图推翻雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安总统的政府。政变失败的后果至今仍在影响着土耳其。 DW回头看了看。 那是2016年7月15日晚上，炎热的夏日即将结束。许多人与朋友或家人一起度过周五晚上，期待周末的到来。没有任何迹象表明土耳其即将发生根本性转变。 然后，仅仅几个小时后，坦克就驶过街道。战斗机飞越安卡拉和伊斯坦布尔。士兵们封锁了连接欧洲和亚洲的博斯普鲁斯海峡大桥。安卡拉议会遭到炮轰。土耳其总统雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安通过视频通话呼吁公众走上街头，制止政变。 政变当晚失败，但其政治后果至今仍在影响着这个国家。 土耳其政府指责居伦运动策划了政变。其创始人、穆斯林神职人员法土拉·葛兰曾被认为是埃尔多安的亲密盟友。他们共同在遏制土耳其军方的政治影响力和扩大埃尔多安的权力方面发挥了关键作用。后来，联盟分崩离析。 到2016年，居伦已在美国流亡多年。政府指责居伦数十年来带着追随者渗透到司法、警察、军队和其他国家机构，试图破坏国家。居伦及其追随者否认参与政变。许多据称与葛兰有联系的高级军事官员被捕。居伦于 2024 年在美国去世，享年 83 岁。 在土耳其，7 月 15 日现在是国定假日。原博斯普鲁斯海峡大桥更名为“7月15日烈士桥”。它纪念当晚丧生的人们。据官方数据，共有 253 人死亡，其中大多数是平民。许多街道、广场和学校也有“7月15日”的名字。 然而，周年纪念不仅仅是为了纪念遇难者。这也标志着一个深刻的政治转折点。居伦运动被指定为恐怖组织，其所谓的支持者大部分来自国家机器。 政变六天后，议会批准了紧急状态。最初期限为三个月，后来七次延长，直到2018年7月19日才结束。这两年，总统主要通过紧急法令施政，共颁布了32项法令。 这些政治清洗的后果是巨大的。超过125,000名公务员和武装部队成员被解雇。根据官方数据，大约...

reflection.en: A coup attempt challenges the very fabric of established governance and the order it maintains. This event reminds us that all authority, whether we agree with its specific form or not, is ultimately permitted by Yahweh. The lasting changes in Turkey underscore the profound impact that the exercise of power has on a nation's destiny.
reflection.zh: 一场政变企图挑战既有治理结构及其所维护的秩序。这事件提醒我们，所有的权柄，无论我们是否认同其具体形式，最终都蒙雅伟所允许。土耳其持久的变革，突显了权力行使对一个国家命运的深远影响。

title.en: US troop withdrawal from Iraq set for September 30
title.zh: 美国计划于9月30日从伊拉克撤军

summary.en: The United States is scheduled to withdraw its troops from Iraq by September 30, a move contingent on the disarmament of powerful Iran-backed militias operating within the country.
summary.zh: 美国计划于9月30日从伊拉克撤军，此举与解除伊拉克境内有影响力的伊朗支持的民兵武装有关。

body.en:
The planned US withdrawal is linked to the disarmament of influential Iran-backed militias in Iraq.

US  troops are set to fully withdraw from Iraq by September 30, the country's prime minister, Ali al-Zaidi, said at a meeting with President Donald Trump in Washington.

"Well, we don't think we need the military there anymore," Trump said at the White House.

Previously, about 2,500 US troops were deployed in Iraq, carrying out counter-Islamic State operations, but that number has declined in recent months.

Al-Zaidi's government has tied the planned US withdrawal to the disarming of powerful Iran-backed militias.

"On September 30th, American forces will leave, and American companies will enter," Zaidi said. "After 30 September, we will not allow any entity to bear arms outside the state."

The main focus of al-Zaidi's trip to Washington is securing major US investment in his country's oil, gas, and power sectors.

During the Oval Office meeting, al-Zaidi previewed an announcement of an "economic partnership" between the two countries.

"We're going to be doing a lot of deals," Trump said. "We're going to create a lot of jobs for both countries, and we're going to be taking out a lot of oil," Trump said, without giving details.

Two Iraqi officials said Iraq, Chevron, TI Capital, and Qatar's UCC are set to sign a deal Friday to build a 2 million-barrel-per-day oil pipeline linking Basra to Haditha and extending to ports in Turkey and Syria.

title.en: US-Iraq relations: Can Iran-allied militias be disarmed?
title.zh: 美国与伊拉克关系：伊朗盟友民兵能否被解除武装？

summary.en: US and Iraqi officials are set to discuss the disarmament of Iran-allied militias in Iraq, with some groups having already expressed willingness to surrender their weapons. The talks will also consider the potential impact on the broader US-Iran conflict.
summary.zh: 美国和伊拉克官员将讨论解除伊拉克境内伊朗盟友民兵的武装，一些团体已表示愿意交出武器。会谈还将考虑这对更广泛的美伊冲突可能产生的影响。

body.en:
When Donald Trump meets Iraq's new PM today, they are likely to discuss disarming Iran's allies in Iraq. Some have already pledged to give up their guns. But is that likely? And will it influence the US-Iran war?

When Iraq's new Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has talks in the White House on Tuesday, it is highly likely he'll discuss more than one uncomfortable topic. On the table is what is potentially the most uncomfortable subject of all, given the US-Iran war: the role that Iran-affiliated paramilitaries play in Iraq .

Most of the paramilitaries, often grouped together as the Popular Mobilization Front, or  PMF, were first formed in 2014 when religious leaders called upon able-bodied men to fight the extremist group known as the  "Islamic State." They now number around 240,000 fighters and have an annual budget of about $3.5 billion (€3 billion).

Some — but not all — PMF factions are considered part of Iran's so-called "Axis of Resistance," which also includes Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen and Hamas in Gaza. During the ongoing conflict between Iran and the US , certain PMF groups are thought to be behind  attacks on US bases in Iraq , Kuwait and Jordan.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio addressed the issue while in the United Arab Emirates last month.

"You can't have the end of hostilities and conflicts in the region as long as Iranian proxies are launching missiles and drones from Iraq and are participating in terrorism," Rubio told reporters.

Over the past year, the US has increased pressure on the Iraqi government to tackle this issue, including by designating several more PMF factions "foreign terrorist organizations," imposing sanctions on businesses associated with the PMF, threatening to block Iraq's oil revenues via US banks, and by withholding foreign currency shipments.

The Iraqi government has responded by saying that, by the end of September, all arms should be brought under the control of the state and that any groups that don't agree will be prosecuted.

In late May, influential cleric Muqtada al-Sadr ordered his armed faction, Saraya al-Salam (in English, peace brigades), to hand over weapons to the state. Around a week later, the Iraqi government said it had received information on personnel, weapons and equipment.

In early June, two other Iraqi paramilitaries — Asaib Ahl al-Haq (in English, league of the righteous) and Kataib Imam Ali (the Imam Ali brigades) — also agreed to end organizational ties to the PMF and to eventually transfer weapons and personnel to the state.

title.en: Bangkok pub fire death toll rises to at least 30 as leaders vow to improve safety standards
title.zh: 曼谷酒吧火灾死亡人数升至至少30人，领导人誓言改进安全标准

summary.en: A pub fire in Bangkok has tragically claimed at least 30 lives, with dozens more critically injured. Following the incident, leaders have pledged to enhance safety standards.
summary.zh: 曼谷一家酒吧发生火灾，造成至少30人死亡，另有数十人伤势严重。事件发生后，领导人承诺将改进安全标准。

body.en:
The death toll from a devastating fire at a live music pub in Thailand's capital climbed to 30 on Tuesday, officials said, as Bangkok's governor vowed stricter inspections and police investigated possible negligence and safety breaches.

The blaze, one of the deadliest in recent years in Thailand, tore through the Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao pub in the city's northern Chatuchak area close to midnight on Sunday , with witnesses describing an explosion, a horizontal burst of fire and smoke engulfing the single-story venue.

There were 24 people in critical condition on Tuesday and dozens more who were treated had been discharged. Three people hospitalised after the fire had since died, according to officials.

A spokesperson for the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said on Tuesday morning it did not appear that any Australians had been affected.

"We stand ready to provide consular assistance if required," the spokesperson said.

The pub, located at a busy intersection next to train stations and two shopping malls, is one of a cluster of similar bars often crowded on weekend nights, serving food, alcohol and offering live music and televised football.

Authorities say an electrical short circuit in a ceiling air conditioner could have triggered the fire in the pub, which underwent a safety inspection in April. Police are investigating whether exits were obstructed and the use of flammable materials for stage decorations and soundproofing.

"We've set up a committee to investigate the truth, what should be improved and what rules should be changed," Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt told a press conference on Tuesday.

Police said 34 people had been interviewed so far and charges would be considered after facts and evidence had been gathered. The owner is among those being treated in an intensive care unit.

At a Bangkok morgue on Tuesday, rescue workers were seen moving the coffin of one of the victims, surrounded by television cameras and a throng of reporters as emotional family members and friends arrived to collect the body.

Outside Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao, some of the relatives were mourning those killed as forensics personnel gathered evidence from the scene.

On its Facebook page, the pub apologised over the fire and said it was cooperating fully with the investigation.

"We apologise deeply over the very sad events that took place and express our condolences to the families of those who lost their lives and send our support to those injured," it said in a post that had hundreds of comments, many expressing anger and questioning its safety measures.

title.en: Trump claimed Iran's nuclear sites were 'obliterated'. Now another is in his sights
title.zh: 特朗普声称伊朗核设施已“被摧毁”，如今又盯上另一处

summary.en: Former President Trump claimed Iran's nuclear sites were "obliterated," but a newly targeted site is reportedly buried 600m under granite, making it impervious to even the most powerful US bunker-buster bombs.
summary.zh: 前总统特朗普曾声称伊朗的核设施已被“摧毁”，但据报道，一个新锁定的核设施深埋在600米花岗岩下，即使是美国最强大的钻地弹也无法触及。

body.en:
A year after US President Donald Trump declared Iran's nuclear sites had been "obliterated", his latest target is drawing attention to a facility that survived both phases of the war untouched — and raising questions about why it's now in his sights.

On Monday, Trump threatened to destroy Pickaxe Mountain, a buried nuclear site near Natanz in north-central Iran where Western intelligence suspects Iran is building an undeclared enrichment facility.

"We're going to take out Pickaxe Mountain. Tell the Iranians to be ready," he said on Monday.

"We're watching (Pickaxe Mountain) closely. We see no activity there. They're not doing well with their nuclear situation. Every time we hear about it, we blow it up. So they don't like talking about it."

The threat comes as just last week, Trump said Iran "will never have a nuclear weapon" and that its stockpile of enriched uranium was now "so far under a mountain" that it was unreachable by anyone except the US.

That follows comments last June, where Trump declared "all" nuclear sites in Iran had been "obliterated", raising a key question: If Iran's nuclear sites were obliterated last year, why is a previously untouched one now a key target?

Pickaxe Mountain is a heavily fortified site near Iran's already-damaged Natanz facility, housing two deeply buried tunnel complexes suspected of containing uranium enrichment capabilities and stockpiles.

Experts have assessed its depth at about 600m below granite, meaning it's beyond the reach of even the most powerful 'bunker-buster' bombs in the US arsenal.

The site was not among the three sites — Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan — targeted by US airstrikes last June, which were believed to house Iranian nuclear facilities .

"Monumental damage was done to all nuclear sites in Iran, as shown by satellite images," Trump said on 25 June 2025. "Obliteration is an accurate term!"

Construction at Pickaxe Mountain began in 2020 and has sped up since June last year — with the Iranian government describing the site as a centrifuge assembly plant.

As of June 2025, the facility was not assessed as operational — something the Institute of Science and International Security says could have been a "key reason why the site was not attacked by airstrikes in the June war".

The institute said satellite analysis and monitoring have raised questions about the "the nuclear activities Iran has planned for the site, specifically whether it includes plans for an enrichment plant".

Pickaxe Mountain isn't the only thing to have survived the alleged "obliteration".

title.en: China economic growth falls sharply, missing target
title.zh: 中国经济增长大幅下滑，未能达到目标

summary.en: China's economic growth has significantly slowed, missing its target due to weak domestic demand and the impact of the Iran war on global oil prices, despite strong export performance.
summary.zh: 由于国内需求疲软以及伊朗战争对油价的影响，中国经济增长大幅放缓，未能达到预期目标，尽管出口表现强劲。

body.en:
China's economic growth slowed sharply between the start of April and end of June as weak domestic demand and the Iran war's impact on oil prices overshadowed the country's strong exports.

Official gross domestic product (GDP) figures showed the world's second largest economy grew in the second quarter by 4.3%, below Beijing's annual target, and after a 5% rise in the first quarter.

It comes a day after government data showed that China's exports jumped by 27% in June compared to a year earlier.

In March, China cut the growth target to a range of 4.5%-5% , its lowest economic expansion goal since 1991, a move some analysts say gives officials more flexibility in managing the economy.

The announcement represents the first full quarter of GDP data since the start of the Iran war on 28 February and marks the lowest quarterly expansion since the end of 2022, as China was emerging from its strict Covid-19 restrictions.

"The are more external instability and uncertainty factors," China's National Bureau of Statistics said in a release accompanying the figures.

It also noted an imbalance between strong supply and weak demand in the domestic economy.

Separate data released on Wednesday highlighted the economic challenges Beijing is facing at home - including a long-running property market slump and weak consumer spending.

New home prices contracted again, although the 0.1% fall in June was at a slightly slower pace than the previous month.

Fabien Yip, a market analyst at investment platform IG told the BBC that China's businesses are absorbing higher energy and raw materials costs "because demand at the till is too weak to bear it".

The situation will become more difficult to manage the longer the Iran war goes on, she added.

Customs data for June, which was released on Tuesday, showed that China's tech exports were boosted by soaring global demand for semiconductors to power artificial intelligence (AI) data centres.

Surging demand for Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) also gave a major boost to China's exports - with monthly car exports topping one million for the first time.
body.zh: 由于国内需求疲软和伊朗战争对油价的影响掩盖了中国强劲的出口，中国的经济增长在四月初至六月底大幅放缓。 官方国内生产总值(GDP)数据显示，继第一季度增长5%之后，世界第二大经济体第二季度增长4.3%，低于北京的年度目标。 一天前，政府数据显示，中国 6 月份出口同比增长 27%。 3月份，中国将增长目标下调至4.5%-5%，这是自1991年以来的最低经济扩张目标，一些分析师表示，此举让官员在管理经济方面拥有更大的灵活性。 该公告代表了自 2 月 28 日伊朗战争爆发以来第一个完整季度的 GDP 数据，也标志着中国正在摆脱严格的 Covid-19 限制之际，自 2022 年底以来的最低季度扩张。 “外部不稳定和不确定因素较多，”中国国家统计局在发布的数据中表示。 报告还指出，国内经济供给旺盛与需求疲软之间存在不平衡。 周三公布的另一份数据突显了北京在国内面临的经济挑战，包括房地产市场长期低迷和消费者支出疲软。 新房价格再次收缩，但 6 月份降幅为 0.1%，降幅较上月略有放缓。 投资平台IG的市场分析师Fabien Yip告诉BBC，中国企业正在吸收更高的能源和原材料成本，“因为收银台的需求太弱而无法承受”。 她补充说，伊朗战争持续的时间越长，局势就越难以控制。 周二公布的 6 月份海关数据显示，全球对为人工智能 (AI) 数据中心提供动力的半导体需求飙升，推动了中国的科技出口。 中国电动汽车（EV）需求的激增也极大地推动了中国的出口——每月汽车出口量首次突破100万辆。

title.en: China detains US scientist who studied North Korea nuclear tests
title.zh: 中国拘留研究朝鲜核试验的美国科学家

summary.en: A US scientist, Chen Youlin, who researched North Korea's nuclear tests, has been detained in China for nearly two years on spying charges, according to his family who claim he is wrongfully held.
summary.zh: 据陈友林的家人称，这位研究朝鲜核试验的美国科学家在中国因间谍罪名被拘留近两年，家人表示他被错误关押。

body.en:
China has detained a US seismologist who tracks nuclear tests for nearly two years on espionage charges, his family says.

Chen Youlin, 54, was arrested in November 2024 during a trip to Beijing to visit family, according to hostage advocacy group Global Reach. The family decided to speak out after they saw no sign of Beijing freeing Chen.

His wife Rong Yufang, also a seismologist, said Chen worked closely with Chinese colleagues, and the allegations are "both wrong and inconsistent with the public and collaborative nature of the work that he has done".

His published work centres on North Korea, a close friend of China and long sanctioned for its nuclear weapons programme and underground tests.

It is unclear if and how Chen's work touched on Beijing's nuclear programme. US intelligence suggests that China is developing a new arsenal and has conducted secret tests, which Beijing denies.

When asked about the case at a daily press briefing on Tuesday, China's foreign ministry said its "judicial authorities handle cases in accordance with the law".

"There is no such thing as so-called wrongful detention," the ministry's spokesman Lin Jian said. In China, espionage convictions can lead to life imprisonment or death.

"I have not been able to speak with my husband for over 600 days and am concerned for his health and well-being," Rong said in a statement through Global Reach.

In an interview with Reuters, she said Chinese authorities interrogated her husband more than 100 times on his work and that he wasn't allowed to see a lawyer for the first 13 months of his detention.

Born in China, Chen became a US citizens in 2011. He lives in Boston, Massachusetts.

He specialised in using seismological data to identify nuclear tests, and undertook several projects funded by the US government. Rong said he his work with colleagues in China was always done "transparently".

"He is doing precisely the kind of people-to-people engagement that the Chinese government says it wants," she added.

Chen's work included a study in December 2020 that looked at seismic data recorded across Asia, including China, to improve methods for nuclear-test monitoring and yield estimation.

According to Global Reach, there are "suspicions within the US government that Chen's arrest was spurred by China's conduct of nuclear tests in violation of the Comprehensive Nuclear Test Ban Treaty".

The group said Chen's expertise would give China "an opportunity to learn as much as possible about US seismic detection methodologies so they can establish countermeasures that allow them to circumvent the treaty".

body.zh: 一名追踪核试验的美国地震学家的家人称，中国以间谍罪名将其拘留了近两年。 据人质权益倡导组织 Global Reach 称，54 岁的陈友林于 2024 年 11 月前往北京探亲时被捕。在看到北京没有释放陈的迹象后，家人决定发声。 他的妻子荣玉芳也是一名地震学家，她表示陈与中国同事密切合作，这些指控“既错误又不符合他所做工作的公开性和协作性”。 他出版的作品以朝鲜为中心，朝鲜是中国的亲密朋友，因其核武器计划和地下试验而长期受到制裁。 目前还不清楚陈的工作是否以及如何触及北京的核计划。美国情报显示，中国正在开发新的核武库并进行了秘密试验，但北京否认了这一点。 中国外交部在周二的每日新闻发布会上被问及此案时表示，“司法机关依法办案”。 公安部新闻发言人林健表示，不存在所谓的错误拘留。在中国，间谍罪可能会被判处无期徒刑或死刑。 荣在 Global Reach 发表的一份声明中表示：“我已经 600 多天无法与丈夫交谈，我很担心他的健康和福祉。” 她在接受路透社采访时表示，中国当局就她丈夫的工作问题对他进行了 100 多次审讯，而且在被拘留的前 13 个月里，他不被允许会见律师。 陈出生于中国，于 2011 年成为美国公民。他住在马萨诸塞州波士顿。 他专门研究利用地震数据识别核试验，并承担了多个由美国政府资助的项目。荣说，他与中国同事的工作总是“透明”地进行。 “他所做的正是中国政府所希望的那种民间交往，”她补充道。 陈的工作包括 2020 年 12 月的一项研究，该研究考察了包括中国在内的亚洲地区记录的地震数据，以改进核试验监测和产量估计的方法。 据Global Reach报道，“美国政府内部怀疑陈的被捕是因为中国违反《全面禁止核试验条约》进行核试验”。 该组织表示，陈的专业知识将使中国“有机会尽可能多地了解美国的地震探测方法，以便他们能够制定规避该条约的对策”。 该条约旨在禁止地球上的所有核爆炸试验，但一些“有核能力”国家尚未批准该条约。其中包括美国和中国，两国都...

title.en: Inside the secret Laos shops selling pangolin scales, bear bile and tiger bones to tourists
title.zh: 老挝秘密商店向游客出售穿山甲鳞片、熊胆和虎骨

summary.en: Covert footage has revealed crime networks operating secret souvenir shops in Laos, facilitating a booming illegal wildlife trade. These shops are reportedly targeting a new influx of Chinese tourists, selling items like pangolin scales, bear bile, and tiger bones.
summary.zh: 秘密拍摄的录像揭示了犯罪网络在老挝经营秘密纪念品商店，助长了蓬勃发展的非法野生动物贸易。据报道，这些商店以新涌入的中国游客为目标，销售穿山甲鳞片、熊胆和虎骨等物品。

body.en: Covert footage obtained by the Guardian shows how crime networks are using front souvenir shops to hide a booming wildlife trade targeted at a new influx of Chinese tourists The shop is dark and deserted. This shop is part of an organised crime network. What is being sold is highly illegal and incredibly unethical. Anyone wandering in would see large bags of specialist tea, local coffee, trinkets and cigarettes on the shelves. But the photographs of wild animals adorning the walls offer a clue to what is truly for sale here. Continue reading...

reflection.en: This report on the illegal wildlife trade reminds us that the earth and all its creatures belong to Yahweh, not to be exploited for human gain. Our role is one of stewardship, recognizing the inherent value of creation as Yahweh's own. Such trade disregards this sacred trust, causing immense suffering and ecological harm.
reflection.zh: 这篇关于非法野生动物贸易的报道提醒我们，地球及其所有生物都属于雅伟，不应被人类为了一己私利而剥削。我们的角色是管家，承认受造物作为雅伟自有之物的内在价值。这种贸易无视了这份神圣的托付，造成了巨大的痛苦和生态破坏。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Undercover in Laos: how Chinese tourism fuels animal trafficking – video
title.zh: 老挝卧底调查：中国旅游业如何助长动物贩运——视频

summary.en: A new report reveals that the booming Chinese tourism industry in Laos is directly linked to a surge in illegal wildlife trafficking. Pangolin scales, rhino horn, and elephant ivory are openly sold in secret shops and restaurants, facilitated by increased visitor numbers due to a new high-speed rail line.
summary.zh: 一份新报告显示，老挝蓬勃发展的中国旅游业与非法野生动物贩运的激增直接相关。穿山甲鳞片、犀牛角和大象象牙在秘密商店和餐馆公开出售，这得益于新高铁线路带来的游客数量增加。

body.en: Chinese tourism is booming in Laos and the illegal wildlife trade is booming with it. Pangolin scales, rhino horn and elephant ivory are all being sold at secret shops and restaurants as a new high-speed rail line brings millions of visitors to the country. Working with Chinese activists, the Guardian goes undercover to investigate the criminal networks profiting from this trade and to reveal how wildlife trafficking is pushing the critically endangered pangolin ever closer to extinction Continue reading...
body.zh: 中国旅游业在老挝蓬勃发展，非法野生动物贸易也随之蓬勃发展。随着新的高铁线路为该国带来数百万游客，穿山甲鳞片、犀牛角和象牙都在秘密商店和餐馆出售。 《卫报》与中国活动人士合作，秘密调查从这种贸易中获利的犯罪网络，并揭露野生动物贩运如何将极度濒危的穿山甲推向灭绝继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report highlights how the pursuit of illicit gain can lead to the exploitation of vulnerable species and ecosystems. When the love of money becomes a driving force, it can blind us to the ethical and environmental consequences of our actions, harming both creation and human integrity.
reflection.zh: 这份报告揭示了对不义之财的追求如何导致对脆弱物种和生态系统的剥削。当贪爱钱财成为主导力量时，它会使我们对行为的伦理和环境后果视而不见，从而损害创造物和人类的正直。

verse.textEn: For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil.
verse.textZh: 贪财是万恶之根。

title.en: China’s monthly car ‌exports top 1m for first time as overall trade soars
title.zh: 中国月度汽车出口首次突破100万辆，整体贸易额飙升

summary.en: China's monthly car exports exceeded 1 million units for the first time in June, contributing to a soaring overall trade volume. The country is likely to match or surpass last year's record trade surplus of $1 trillion, which may lead to new tariffs from the US and EU.
summary.zh: 中国6月份的汽车月出口量首次突破100万辆，推动整体海外出货量飙升。该国很可能达到或超过去年1万亿美元的创纪录贸易顺差，这可能导致美国和欧盟征收新的关税。

body.en: Country risks new tariffs from US and EU as it looks likely to match or beat last year’s record surplus of $1tn Business live – latest updates China’s monthly car ‌exports topped 1m for the first time in June as overall overseas shipments from the world’s second biggest economy rose 27%. Official Chinese customs data showed that a stronger-than-expected trade performance kept China on track to match or beat last year’s record trade surplus of $1tn (£748bn), achieved despite Donald Trump’s curtailed tariff war. Continue reading...
body.zh: 该国面临美国和欧盟征收新关税的风险，因为它可能会追平或超过去年创纪录的 1 万亿美元顺差 Business live – 最新动态 中国的月度汽车出口量在 6 月份首次突破 100 万辆，全球第二大经济体的海外总出货量增长了 27%。中国官方海关数据显示，强于预期的贸易表现使中国有望追平或超越去年创纪录的1万亿美元（7,480亿英镑）贸易顺差，尽管唐纳德·特朗普缩减了关税战，但仍实现了这一目标。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This news highlights a nation's impressive economic output and trade surplus, yet also points to potential international friction. Deuteronomy 8:18 reminds us that Yahweh is the ultimate source of the ability to produce wealth. This perspective invites reflection on how national prosperity can be stewarded not just for accumulation, but for purposes that...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了一个国家令人瞩目的经济产出和贸易顺差，但也指出了潜在的国际摩擦。申命记8:18提醒我们，雅伟是赐予我们创造财富能力的最终源头。这一视角促使我们思考，国家繁荣如何不仅是为了积累财富，更是为了促进国家间和平与共同福祉的目的而加以管理。

verse.textEn: Remember Yahweh your God, for it is he who gives you the ability to produce wealth.
verse.textZh: 你要记念雅伟你的神，因为得货财的力量是他给你的。

title.en: The Guardian view on Volkswagen’s crisis: another wake-up call for Germany and the EU | Editorial
title.zh: 《卫报》关于大众汽车危机的观点：给德国和欧盟的又一次警醒 | 社论

summary.en: The Guardian editorial highlights the need for strong measures to safeguard European industries from what it describes as unfair competition. It warns that failure to act could lead to social unrest amidst growing economic insecurity, citing a significant trade surplus China holds with the European Union in...
summary.zh: 《卫报》社论指出，需要采取强有力措施保护欧洲工业免受其所称的不公平竞争。社论警告说，如果不采取行动，日益增长的不安全感可能导致社会冲突，并提到中国在制成品贸易中对欧盟享有显著顺差。

body.en: Robust action is needed to protect European industries from unfair competition. The alternative is social strife amid growing insecurity According to a recent analysis , China enjoys a surplus in its manufactured goods trade with the European Union that is roughly equivalent to Italy’s national income. That trade disparity, it is estimated, continues to grow by about 30% each year. The stark implication, according to a paper from Centre for European Reform, is that Europe, with Germany in the frontline, risks “deindustrialisation at China’s hand”. The gravity of the threat was grimly evident in the car industry last week, as Volkswagen’s supervisory board met to discuss radical proposals to cut 100,000 jobs – around a sixth of the company’s global workforce – and close plants. Taking into account indirect as well as direct employment, the automotive sector is responsible for around 3m jobs in Germany. But manufacturers in the country’s flagship industry have found themselves in a triple bind. Continue reading...
body.zh: 需要采取强有力的行动来保护欧洲工业免受不公平竞争的影响。另一种选择是日益不安全的社会冲突 根据最近的分析，中国在与欧盟的制成品贸易中享有顺差，大致相当于意大利的国民收入。据估计，贸易差距每年继续扩大约 30%。欧洲改革中心的一篇论文指出，最明显的含义是，以德国为首的欧洲面临着“中国去工业化”的风险。上周，大众汽车监事会召开会议，讨论了裁员 10 万人（约占该公司全球员工人数的六分之一）和关闭工厂的激进提议，这一威胁的严重性在汽车行业中显而易见。考虑到间接和直接就业，汽车行业为德国创造了约 300 万个就业岗位。但该国旗舰行业的制造商发现自己陷入了三重困境。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for "robust action" against "unfair competition" in trade echoes a timeless concern for justice in commerce. Yahweh delights in honest dealings and just weights, reminding us that economic relationships between nations should reflect fairness and integrity. When competition is perceived as unfair, it can lead to instability and hardship for many,...
reflection.zh: 呼吁对贸易中的“不公平竞争”采取“强有力行动”，反映了对商业公正的永恒关注。雅伟喜悦诚实的交易和公正的砝码，提醒我们国与国之间的经济关系应体现公平和正直。当竞争被视为不公时，可能导致许多人的不稳定和困苦，这突显了全球贸易需要伦理原则的指导。

verse.textEn: Yahweh detests dishonest scales, but accurate weights find favor with him.
verse.textZh: 诡诈的天平为雅伟所憎恶；公平的法码为他所喜悦。

title.en: Weather tracker: Unusually warm rivers affect French nuclear power plants
title.zh: 天气追踪：异常温暖的河流影响法国核电站

summary.en: Unusually high temperatures and below-average rainfall across western and central Europe have led to warm rivers, putting pressure on waterways used to cool French nuclear power plants.
summary.zh: 西欧和中欧大部分地区异常高温和低于平均水平的降雨量导致河流温度升高，给用于冷却法国核电站的水道带来了压力。

body.en: High temperatures and below average rainfall put pressure on waterways used to cool reactors Above average temperatures combined with below average rainfall across much of western and central Europe during June and the first half of July have placed increasing pressure on rivers, ecosystems and energy infrastructure. Persistent high pressure brought prolonged sunshine, suppressed rainfall and enhanced evaporation, causing river levels to fall and water temperatures to increase. These unusually warm rivers are affecting electricity generation in France, as several nuclear power stations rely on river water for cooling. Under French environmental regulations, operators must limit the amount of heat discharged back into rivers, meaning electricity output may need to be reduced when water temperatures become too high. Continue reading...
body.zh: 高温和低于平均水平的降雨量给用于冷却反应堆的水道带来了压力。6月和7月上半月，西欧和中欧大部分地区的气温高于平均水平，降雨量低于平均水平，给河流、生态系统和能源基础设施带来了越来越大的压力。持续的高压带来日照时间延长、降雨减少、蒸发加剧，导致河流水位下降、水温升高。这些异常温暖的河流正在影响法国的发电，因为一些核电站依靠河水进行冷却。根据法国环境法规，运营商必须限制排回河流的热量，这意味着当水温过高时可能需要减少电力输出。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The news of unusually warm rivers affecting power plants reminds us that creation itself can feel the strain of environmental changes. Romans 8:22 speaks of creation groaning, a poignant image for the pressure waterways are experiencing. This calls us to consider our interconnectedness with the natural world and our role in its well-being.
reflection.zh: 河流异常温暖影响核电站的新闻提醒我们，受环境变化影响，受造界本身也会感到压力。罗马书8:22提到受造之物一同叹息，这生动地描绘了水道所承受的压力。这促使我们思考与自然世界的相互关联，以及我们在其福祉中所扮演的角色。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: China’s graduate glut: millions enter a job market with little use for them
title.zh: 中国毕业生过剩：数百万人进入就业市场却无用武之地

summary.en: China is experiencing a record number of university graduates entering a job market with low demand for their skills, particularly in entry-level tech roles affected by AI and automation. This coincides with the traditional graduation season, a time of transition for students.
summary.zh: 中国正面临创纪录数量的大学毕业生进入就业市场，但他们的技能需求有限，尤其是在受人工智能和自动化影响的入门级科技岗位。这恰逢传统的毕业季，是大学生们过渡的时期。

body.en: Record numbers find there is little demand for their skills, as entry-level tech roles are hit by AI and automation This time of year is graduation season in China: traditionally a bittersweet period of solemn goodbyes and family celebrations as university students transition from campus life into adulthood. Now it also increasingly represents trepidation about the future. Each year, millions more graduates are thrust into China’s already saturated jobs market. The situation for this year’s cohort, flooding into an increasingly crowded pool of applicants fighting for an insufficient number of positions, is arguably the bleakest yet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 创纪录的数字发现，由于入门级技术职位受到人工智能和自动化的打击，对他们的技能的需求很少。每年的这个时候是中国的毕业季：传统上，随着大学生从校园生活过渡到成年，这是一个苦乐参半的时期，举行庄严的告别和家庭庆祝活动。现在它也越来越代表着对未来的恐惧。每年，都有数以百万计的毕业生涌入中国已经饱和的就业市场。今年的申请者涌入越来越拥挤的人群，争夺职位数量不足，这可以说是迄今为止最惨淡的情况。继续阅读...

reflection.en: For millions of graduates facing a challenging job market, the news of limited demand for their skills can be disheartening. Colossians 3:23 reminds us that whatever work we undertake, we are called to do it heartily, as for Yahweh and not for human employers. This perspective can bring dignity and purpose to every effort, even when external circumstances...
reflection.zh: 对于数百万面临严峻就业市场的毕业生来说，技能需求有限的消息可能令人沮丧。歌罗西书3:23提醒我们，无论我们做什么，都要从心里做，像是给雅伟做的，不是给人做的。这种视角能为我们所做的每一份努力带来尊严和意义，即便外部环境充满挑战。

verse.textEn: Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for Yahweh, not for human masters.
verse.textZh: 无论做什么，都要从心里做，像是给主做的，不是给人做的。

title.en: Nearly two million evacuated as Typhoon Bavi barrels towards China
title.zh: 强台风巴威逼近中国，近两百万人被疏散

summary.en: A powerful typhoon, Bavi, is approaching China, prompting the evacuation of nearly two million people. In the Philippines, heavy rains associated with the storm have already caused two landslides, resulting in 17 fatalities.
summary.zh: 强台风巴威正逼近中国，导致近两百万人被疏散。在菲律宾，受台风带来的强降雨影响，已发生两起山体滑坡，造成17人死亡。

body.en:
China evacuated more than 1.8 million people on Saturday as Typhoon Bavi churned toward the major eastern city of Wenzhou after pummelling Japan's southern Sakishima island chain with heavy rain and violent winds and brushing past northern Taiwan.

Even as Bavi continues to slow and weaken on its northwesterly path over cooler seas, the typhoon is still a potent risk due to the sheer volume of moisture it holds within its rain bands, about the size of France from end to end.

Bavi had maximum sustained winds of 144 km/h, equivalent to Category 1 on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale, and was about 200km southeast of Wenling in the eastern province of Zhejiang as of Saturday night (AEST), according to the National Meteorological Center.

Bavi is forecast to make landfall around Wenzhou, home to some 10 million people, early on Sunday.

State media said more than 1.7 million people had been evacuated across Zhejiang province, where Wenzhou is located, and more than 100,000 in neighbouring Fujian province.

"I'm a little worried, but I think it'll be OK. We've been through typhoons before. We'll get through it," said Wenzhou resident Huang Xinghuan, 50, who was out buying groceries at a traditional wet market before it closed ahead of the typhoon.

Huang said his family had stocked about two to three days' worth of water. "I think supplies are well guaranteed now. There's no need to panic or stockpile a lot of food or other supplies," he added.

While Japan and Taiwan have not so far reported any deaths from the typhoon, 17 people died in the Philippines due to heavy rains brought by an enhanced southwest monsoon, worsened by Bavi's impact.

Taiwan's fire department said 87 people had been injured, mostly falls from motorcycles or bicycles, as well as people falling over or being struck by objects.

More than 18,000 households and facilities across Okinawa, Japan lost power as the typhoon pounded Japan's remote southwestern islands, with the Miyako region hardest hit.

Japanese airlines cancelled dozens of flights, affecting more than 26,000 passengers.

"Miyako is taking worst of typhoon Bavi," professional storm-chaser James Reynolds posted on X from Ishigaki on Saturday.

"Conditions on Ishigaki gale force with some overnight gusts to typhoon strength."

In Taiwan, the government evacuated more than 14,000 people from mainly mountainous areas as the island shut down for the approach of Bavi to the north.

While Bavi did not make landfall on Taiwan, the government took precautions to prevent loss of life, given forecasts for almost 1 metre (3 feet) of rain in some areas.

reflection.en: As Typhoon Bavi brings severe weather and tragic loss of life, many face the terrifying prospect of walking through a "valley of the shadow of death." In such moments of profound vulnerability and fear, Yahweh's presence offers a steadfast comfort and courage. Even amidst the storm's fury and the pain of loss, we can trust in His unwavering care.
reflection.zh: 当台风巴威带来恶劣天气和悲惨的生命损失时，许多人面临着走过“死荫的幽谷”的可怕前景。在这样极度脆弱和恐惧的时刻，雅伟的同在提供了坚定的安慰和勇气。即使在风暴的狂怒和失去亲人的痛苦中，我们也能信赖祂坚定不移的看顾。

verse.textEn: Even though I walk through the darkest valley, I will fear no evil, for you are with me.
verse.textZh: 我虽然行过死荫的幽谷，也不怕遭害，因为你与我同在。

title.en: Jacinta Nampijinpa Price rebuked for sharing false claim Labor ‘importing’ Indian migrants
title.zh: 雅辛塔·南皮金帕·普赖斯因分享工党“进口”印度移民的虚假言论而受斥责

summary.en: Northern Territory senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price was rebuked for sharing a social media clip containing a false claim that the Labor party was “importing” Indian migrants. This incident resurrected a controversy that previously led to her removal from the Liberal frontbench.
summary.zh: 北领地参议员雅辛塔·南皮金帕·普赖斯因在社交媒体上分享一段包含工党“进口”印度移民虚假说法的视频而受到指责。这一事件重新引发了去年导致她被自由党前座议员职位解职的争议。

The federal government says it will support Australia's creative sector amid growing concerns about the development of artificial intelligence and data centres, as Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is set to reveal a 'world-first' AI plan.

Albanese is expected to launch the Office of AI at a speech in Sydney on Wednesday, after dozens of Australian artists voiced concerns about the uncertainty of whether Australia-based AI data centres would be granted an exemption from copyright laws.

Speaking to the ABC on Wednesday, Assistant Technology Minister Andrew Charlton said the federal government has "a clear and united position" on the issue.

"Our approach is that we support the Australian creative sector. We are not going to undermine that sector, with a data centre that tries to seek exception," Charlton said.

Charlton, who's been supporting AI investment in Australia, said the government only wanted AI investment "that's in Australia's national interest", and said the prime minister's speech later on Wednesday would set out clear standards for the types of investment Australia would be interested in.

The Office of AI, which will be under the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, will coordinate the development of new Australian standards on AI and its impacts on issues such as energy, copyright, productivity, education and labour rights.

"Australia will be the first country in the world to bring these issues into a single, national framework," Albanese will say.

The announcement comes as several tech giants, including Anthropic, which creates the AI chatbot Claude, seek investment in AI data centres in Australia — amid concerns about their impact on Australian intellectual property.

Anthropic has warned that its $21.6 billion investment in Australia hinges on receiving clarity about copyright and its legal obligations.

Albanese will respond to that concern in his speech, arguing that the right guardrails will attract business.

"Getting this right will enhance our appeal to international investors, by delivering greater clarity and speed for approvals, and a streamlined process for verifying compliance," Albanese will say.

Albanese will say the national framework adds to the government's ongoing design of a digital duty of care and the mitigation of risks posed by AI to children and national security.

"We know that both extremists and state actors already use AI to create propaganda aimed at young people — and to spread disinformation that targets democracies," he will say.

body.en:
Australian superannuation funds have been handed a poor report card after a mystery shopping exercise found call centre staff across the sector were falling short on basic customer care.

The study, published by consumer group Super Consumers Australia on Tuesday, found call centres at 20 of the country's biggest funds delivered inconsistent and unempathetic service that often fell short of basic expectations.

But parts of the sector have pushed back on the findings and methodology of the study.

Super Consumers Australia commissioned customer experience firm Customer Service Benchmarking Australia (CSBA) to run 1,000 mystery shopper calls across the 20 funds between August and October last year, posing as prospective members, non-English-speaking customers' relatives, and people in financial distress.

Not a single fund cracked 55 per cent — well short of the 80 per cent regarded as the "green zone", which indicates optimal performance for customer experience across sectors.

By comparison, utilities, banking, education and local government all scored higher than the super sector.

Consistency was also a problem, with individual scores swinging from as low as 20 per cent to as high as 86 per cent, even within the same fund.

CareSuper came out on top with 55 per cent, followed by Rest Super and TelstraSuper.

Seven in 10 callers from customers in vulnerable or distressing situations rated agents five or lower out of 10 for empathy.

Two funds were excluded from the overall rankings because so many calls didn't get through. AustralianSuper connected only 10 per cent of its calls within 15 minutes, while Team Super connected to 52 per cent, against an 87 per cent average across the rest of the sector.

"Superannuation is mandatory, but good customer service is not. That has to change," Super Consumers Australia CEO Xavier O’Halloran said. "This pilot study shows that, right now, getting the right support can depend on who answers the phone."

"People should not have to beg their super fund for basic help. If your fund is not listening, complain. If poor service keeps happening, consider taking your money elsewhere."

He called for mandatory customer service standards to be implemented for super funds, as is standard in other sectors.

AustralianSuper rejected the findings, saying the study was conducted while it was mid-transition to a new call centre provider.

"Our customer satisfaction scores right now are the highest they've ever been, and our average speed of answer is less than two minutes," an AustralianSuper spokesperson said.
